description: Add the minimal CUTE DSL extension path and replace torch.geqrf for dominant batched n=512 shapes with a blocked Householder QR kernel, staging panels in shared memory, emitting compact H and tau, and falling back for other sizes until correctness is established.

Add the minimal CUTE DSL extension path and build a specialized warp/block QR path for n=32/176/352, reducing PyTorch launch overhead with coalesced column loads and explicit reflector updates while preserving compact Householder output.

Add the minimal CUTE DSL extension path and implement large-matrix QR for n=1024/2048/4096 using communication-avoiding tall-panel blocking with separate panel factorization and batched GEMM-like trailing updates, generating compact H/tau directly.

Implement a real local-only CUTE tiled CAQR path for large n>=512: one CTA per panel tile, shared-memory compact WY Householder, warp norm/tau reductions, and GEMM-style trailing update, falling back to torch only outside validated shapes.

Extend the winning n=32 path with a CUTE DSL medium-size QR for n=176/352 using blocked Householder panels, static per-panel shared memory, and streaming global-memory trailing updates instead of full-matrix shared storage; preserve n=32 unchanged.

Replace one-CTA-per-matrix Householder with a multi-CTA n=512 CUTE tiled CAQR path: split panels across CTAs, use shared-memory tile reductions for norms/dots, and apply reflectors with cooperative trailing-update kernels.

Merge worker1's n=32 and n=176 custom fast paths with worker0's n=512 split panel/update CUTE CTA scaffold; preserve dispatch boundaries and fallback behavior, using local CUTE DSL only for shared tiling helpers.

Build a clean local CUTE combine: preserve worker1's proven n=32/n=176 specializations from 620492a4, replace the old n=512 route with worker0's tile-width-4 n=512 implementation, and avoid regressed n=352 changes.
